 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><B>Dealer Manager Agreement </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial">The Feeder and BXINFRA U.S. entered into an amended and restated dealer manager agreement, as amended and restated and as may be further amended and
restated from time to time (the &#8220;<B>Dealer Manager Agreement</B>&#8221;) with Blackstone Securities Partners L.P. (the &#8220;<B>Dealer Manager</B>&#8221;), a broker-dealer registered with the SEC under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as
amended, and a member of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority. Pursuant to the Dealer Manager Agreement, the Dealer Manager manages the Feeder&#8217;s relationships with third-party brokers engaged by the Dealer Manager to participate in the
distribution of Units, which are referred to as participating brokers, and financial advisors. The Dealer Manager also coordinates the Feeder&#8217;s marketing and distribution efforts with participating brokers and their registered representatives
with respect to communications related to the terms of the Feeder&#8217;s offering, its investment strategies, material aspects of its operations and subscription procedures. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial">The Dealer Manager is entitled to receive unitholder servicing fees monthly in arrears at an annual rate of&nbsp;0.85% of the value of the
Feeder&#8217;s Transactional NAV attributable to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Class&nbsp;S-TE</FONT> Units and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Class&nbsp;S-TE-ACC</FONT></FONT> Units as of the last day of each
month. The Dealer Manager is entitled to receive unitholder servicing fees monthly in arrears at an annual rate of&nbsp;0.25% of the value of the Feeder&#8217;s Transactional NAV attributable to
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Class&nbsp;D-TE</FONT> Units and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Class&nbsp;D-TE-ACC</FONT></FONT> Units as of the last day of each month. In calculating the servicing fees, the
Feeder uses the Transactional NAV before giving effect to any accruals for the servicing fees, redemptions for that month and distributions, if any, payable on the Feeder&#8217;s Units. There are no unitholder servicing fees with respect to <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Class&nbsp;I-TE</FONT> Units and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Class&nbsp;I-TE-ACC</FONT></FONT> Units. The unitholder servicing fees are payable to the Dealer Manager, but the Dealer
Manager anticipates that all of such fees will be retained by, or reallowed (paid) to, participating brokers or other financial intermediaries. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial">The
Feeder accrues the cost of the unitholder servicing fees for the estimated life of the Units, as applicable, as a distribution cost at the time <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Class&nbsp;S-TE,</FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Class&nbsp;S-TE-ACC,</FONT></FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Class&nbsp;D-TE</FONT> and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Class&nbsp;D-TE-ACC</FONT></FONT> Units are sold. Servicing
Fees Payable as of December&nbsp;31, 2025 was $27.6&nbsp;million. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><B>Due to Affiliates </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial">Due to Affiliates consists of cash advances made by Blackstone Holdings Finance Co. L.L.C., a subsidiary of Blackstone, on behalf of the Feeder for the
payment of fund expenses. These amounts are intended to be cash reimbursed by the Feeder and are <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-interest</FONT> bearing. Due to Affiliates also consists of balances the Feeder owes to other <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-consolidated</FONT> entities within BXINFRA. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><B>BXINFRA Lux </B></P>

allowance when it is <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">more-likely-than-not</FONT> that all or a portion of the deferred tax asset may not be realized. The Feeder assesses all available positive and negative evidence, including the amount and
character of future taxable income. Based on its assessment, management has concluded that it is not more-likely-than not that certain deferred tax assets will be realized and therefore, a valuation allowance has been established against those tax
assets.&nbsp;The realizable amount and associated valuation allowance could change in future periods based on updated objective evidence. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial">As of
December&nbsp;31, 2025, the Feeder had aggregate federal income tax net operating losses (&#8220;<B>NOL</B>&#8221;). The Feeder had federal NOLs of $1.0&nbsp;million, of which $1.0&nbsp;million can be carried forward indefinitely. The Feeder had no
aggregate state income tax NOLs. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><B>Uncertain Tax Positions </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial">As of December&nbsp;31, 2025, the Feeder is not aware of any uncertain tax positions that would require recognition in the Consolidated Financial
Statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><B>One Big Beautiful Bill Act </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial">On July&nbsp;4,
2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (&#8220;<B>OBBBA</B>&#8221;) was signed into law in the U.S., introducing a broad range of tax reform provisions affecting businesses, including extending and modifying certain key provisions of the Tax
Cuts&nbsp;&amp; Jobs Act of 2017. In accordance with GAAP, the effects of the enacted tax law changes were recognized in the period of enactment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:4%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial">The OBBBA did not change the U.S. federal corporate income tax rate. The Feeder evaluated the provisions of the law and determined there was no
remeasurement of the deferred tax assets and liabilities and that the OBBBA had no material impact to the Feeder&#8217;s consolidated financial statements as of and for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2025. </P>
